name: LG Electronics India Ltd
title: LG Electronics India Ltd - 544576 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: LG Electronics India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.5% to INR72.33 billion and EBITDA margin expanded 110 bps to 12.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 15.5% YoY to INR72.33 billion, with every key category growing double digits on both volume and value. EBITDA rose 26.2% to INR9.04 billion, with margin up 110 bps YoY to 12.5% on product mix, calibrated price increases and operating leverage. PAT grew 27.2% to INR6.53 billion (8.9% margin). Management highlighted record quarterly exports to over 60 countries, Sri City capex of INR5.88 billion out of INR7.36 billion total, and a fully internally funded plan with no external borrowing.

financial_highlights.change: +110 bps YoY (11.4%); +0.8 pp QoQ per IRO
INR5.88 billion deployed at Sri City

segments.name: Home Appliance and Air Solution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55.77 billion, up 13.6% YoY; segment EBIT up about 13.8% to about INR6.4 billion, margin steady at 11.5%. Premium French door refrigerators, 8 kg+ washing machines and dishwashers grew well ahead of portfolio.

segments.name: Home Entertainment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR16.57 billion, up 22.3% YoY; segment EBIT up 48.5% YoY with margin expanding to 19%. TV revenue grew about 25%; 55-inch and above grew about 53% and now contributes about 50% of TV business.

segments.name: Information Display (within Home Entertainment)
segments.commentary: Management cited LED signage at its highest ever quarterly sales and a 36% market share, about 5 pp ahead of the number 2 player. Growth came from government and corporate orders.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 demand to be broad-based, with TV and washing machines expected to drive H2 growth; AC and refrigerators to benefit from premiumisation and replacement.
Q2 channel stocking underway ahead of Onam, Durga Puja and Diwali; launch pipeline described as full.
Exports: management says it will hit its yearly export target but gave no numeric guidance; export margins are described as better than domestic.
Sri City capitalisation expected to begin in H2 FY27; initial incremental costs expected near term.
Localisation target of 65% over the next 3 to 4 years, from 55.2% in the last full year.
Dividend to be reviewed as Sri City progresses and cash generation strengthens; current year dividend decision was made with capex priorities in mind.
Commercial AC business: management is confident of a 20% CAGR trajectory, as achieved over FY22 to FY25.
capex_capacity: Sri City (Andhra Pradesh): third plant, outlay of INR5,000 crore, deployed in phases over the next few years; compressor production started in Q3 FY27 and room AC production in Q4 FY27 per IRO remarks.
Sri City adds 2 million AC capacity; Greater Noida has 1 million AC capacity and 7 million refrigerator capacity.
Investment expected to almost double manufacturing capacity and position India as an export hub; funded entirely by internal accruals with no external debt.
Pune and Greater Noida plants being expanded for new Essential family sizes and premium products.
Data-centre cooling: mid-scale projects already live using Multi V VRF and chiller systems; hyperscale is at a preliminary stage, with partnerships under evaluation.
demand_pricing: Calibrated price increases were taken in selected categories and absorbed well; further pricing will depend on input costs.
Essential Series sold over 500,000 units in January to June 2026, exceeding plan; margins in line with the B2C portfolio, not dilutive; exported to 22 countries.
Exports grew 30% in Q1; LG now supplies over 60 countries (65 per Co-CSMO) versus 45 to 47 at the time of IPO.

Government notified quantitative restrictions on compressor imports from 8 May: reciprocating compressors restricted up to 60% and rotary compressors up to 70% (per management, against FY25 levels). Management sees this as positive for cost and share.
TV market share is about 26% and OLED share about 59%; 16 new QNED models and Micro RGB TV launched early in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra (J.P. Morgan): How sustainable is Home Entertainment growth, and how much is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said TV grew about 25% for a second straight quarter, with growth from both volume and value; 55-inch and above grew about 53% and now is about 50% of TV business. He called the growth structural and not seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra: Export growth, US and Europe contribution, FY27 export target, and export margins versus domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew 30% in Q1. Two pillars: premium products to key global markets and Essential Series to Asia, Middle East and Africa. Export margins are better than domestic. No numeric FY27 target was given beyond saying the yearly target will be hit.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavani K (Axis): Key growth drivers for FY27 and long-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Soonjoo Seo cited exports scaling, premiumisation across categories (large TVs, French door and side-by-side refrigerators, 8 kg+ washing machines, 5-star inverter ACs), and India's role in the global south strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavani K: What is the impact of the revised compressor import policy, given the Q3 compressor facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaganjeet Singh said the policy is positive: LG has 1 million AC capacity at Greater Noida plus 2 million at Sri City, and 7 million refrigerator capacity at Greater Noida, which is above internal needs. Management expects a cost advantage and share gains in refrigerators and ACs.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama): B2B performance and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said B2B grew strongly; LED signage had its highest ever quarterly sales; commercial AC is expanding distribution and 2-ton 4-star models. Management is confident of a 20% CAGR, as delivered over FY22 to FY25. No Q1 B2B revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: How is raw material cost inflation being managed, and what is the Q2 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaganjeet Singh listed localisation (including a resin localised in Q1), flexible local and import sourcing, multiple suppliers, and value engineering. Calibrated price increases are already taken; further action depends on input costs. No Q2 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Siddharth Bora (Nomura): Category-wise FY27 growth outlook, and is Q1 representative?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Chitkara said all products grew double digits in Q1 and demand is healthy across segments. TV and washing machines are expected to drive H2 growth. No category growth numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Siddharth Bora: Essential Series volume, revenue contribution, further SKUs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurpinderjeet Singh said over 500,000 units were sold in six months, margins are in line with the B2C portfolio, refrigerator range expanded to 225, 251 and 276 litres, and a higher-capacity top loader is planned. No revenue share was given.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Goel (HSBC): Localisation path from 55% and bottlenecks to 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Khanna said localisation was 55.2% in the last full year, improving 2-3 pp a year, with a target of 65% over the next 3 to 4 years. Sri City AC compressors and local side-by-side refrigerator production at Pune are key steps.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Goel: Data-centre cooling readiness and dividend or capital return plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mid-scale data-centre cooling is already live with Multi V and chillers; hyperscale is preliminary, with partner-led routes under evaluation and not a key FY27 driver. Atul Khanna said the dividend was set with capex in mind, funding Sri City from internal accruals, and that the dividend policy will be reviewed as cash generation improves.

risks_watch: Sri City ramp-up: near-term incremental costs before efficiency gains; capitalisation from H2 FY27.
Raw material and component cost inflation and rupee depreciation; management relies on pricing, localisation and sourcing to protect margins.
Dividend payout is constrained by the INR5,000 crore Sri City programme; the review timing is not set.
Sustainability of Home Entertainment margin at 19% after promotional normalisation.
Export growth depends on geopolitical conditions, including the West Asia conflict; no numeric export target given.
Compressor import restrictions: benefits depend on policy implementation and the pace of Sri City ramp-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margin and market share, with the most specific figures given for TV and Home Entertainment. Management was cautious on export targets and hyperscale data-centre opportunities, and vague on the timing of dividends.
key_quotes: On margin, the context is what makes this significant. We expanded margins in a quarter when the entire industry was absorbing raw material cost pressure.
We are not just delivering the result , we are building a business that creates lasti ng value for every stakeholder.
This is a transformational investment that will almost double our manufacturing capacity, significantly strengthen our export capabilities, and position LG India as a future global export hub.

adds.what: Sri City (Andhra Pradesh) third plant, 2 million AC capacity, INR5,000 crore outlay deployed in phases; compressor production started Q3 FY27, room AC productio

growth.why: Management guides to broad-based FY27 growth led by H2 TV and washing machines, a 20% CAGR for commercial AC and exports "significantly" up without numbers, backed by a full launch pipeline, Q2 stocking and Sri City capacity (2 million AC) that only begins capitalising in H2 FY27, so backing is partial rather than clear.
